# Updating Runme and choosing a version

Runme keeps using the installed release when you refresh or open another tab, including offline. A background check downloads updates without activating them. Open **Versions** to follow **stable** or **latest**, pin an exact release ID, browse published releases, or choose a complete cached release. Initially both channels follow successful main commits. Changing a channel or pin downloads a candidate; **Upgrade all tabs** activates it.

## Upgrading with multiple tabs

Stop running cells and finish reviews first. Runme freezes editing, waits for each tab to save its notebooks and App Console draft locally, then hands storage to the new worker and reloads the tabs. Pending Drive work may remain offline; a confirmed local save is sufficient. An error or an unresponsive tab blocks activation. A timeout never counts as permission to discard that tab's changes.

Use **Retry preparation / resume** after fixing the reported problem. Before handoff, **Cancel upgrade** keeps the current release; already prepared tabs reload their confirmed saved state. After handoff starts, Runme must finish or recover that specific transition. You may need to bring a sleeping tab to the foreground. Close it only after preserving its unsaved work.

## Recovery and rollback

**Open recovery in another tab** opens a selector independent of the application bundle. It can choose a complete cached release when the application fails to start. Close failed application tabs after preserving any edits so their membership can be retired. If a candidate's storage startup failed, recovery can select a compatible cached release only when exclusive storage ownership is available. It never steals a lock from a live worker.

Rollback changes application code and keeps current notebook data. It does not restore an old database snapshot, undo remote writes, or undo cell execution. This first compatibility contract supports the current schema only; incompatible releases are rejected. **Remove unused downloads** retains installed, previous, selected, pending, healthy, and live-tab releases. It does not remove notebook storage.

The initial migration from the old app may request that you save/download recovery copies, close all Runme tabs, and reopen. This retires the old service worker and storage owner. Subsequent app upgrades use the coordinated flow above. If the loader itself cannot start, reconnect and close/reopen all Runme tabs so the browser can update it; report the failure with the browser version and URL. Do not clear site data as a routine repair because it includes local notebooks and unsynced changes.

## Agent API

Use `app.releases.help()` in App Console or ExecuteCode. `get()` reports selection, installed release, candidate, participants, phases and storage startup diagnostics. `check({kind:"channel",name:"latest"})` downloads a candidate; `check({kind:"pinned",releaseId:"<full SHA>-<build digest>"})` downloads an exact build. `upgrade()` requests the same coordinated activation as the UI. `retry()`, `cancel()` and `prune()` map to the recovery controls. These APIs never use a sessionStorage backup as proof of a durable notebook save.
